narrative.title: Purging Recalled Batches from the Two-Way Sorter
narrative.scenario: A distribution center's two-way sorter tracks bins of medication batches, and a recall notice flags one batch ID. Every bin carrying that ID must be pulled from the belt without disturbing the order of the rest — whether the bin sits at the intake end, the discharge end, or anywhere between. Because each station knows both neighbours, a pulled bin's two neighbours can re-link to each other directly.
narrative.inputFormat: An array arr of n node values forming the doubly linked list, and an integer key.
narrative.outputFormat: The values of the list after every node equal to key is unlinked, read from the new head.

testCases.explanation: Every station carrying the recalled batch 2 is pulled; the four clean stations keep their relative order.
Removals at the intake end reassign the head itself — after both 4s are pulled, 6 is the new entry point.

hintLevels: Level 1: One traversal is enough — at each station you only need to decide whether it stays on the belt.
Level 2: When a node matches, re-wire its two neighbours to each other; when the match is the current head, move the head forward first.
Level 3: Guard every neighbour access — a match at the tail has no next, and the head pointer must survive even if every node is deleted.
